rounds.proof_sketch: With dim=16384, stride=1024, the loop runs 16 times (i=0,1024,...,15360) for original. Mutant adds i=16384 iteration. After 16 iterations, all threads have idx >= 16384 (thread 0: 16384, thread 255: 17404). Inner condition 'idx+3 < 16384' is FALSE for all threads in the 17th iteration, so no additional work executes.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the loop bound from '<' to '<=' allowing one extra iteration when i=dim=16384. However, by the time this iteration is reached, all threads have advanced their idx values beyond the valid range. Thread 0 has idx=16384, thread 255 has idx=17404, and all intermediate threads have proportionally larger idx values. The inner guard condition 'idx + 3 < (batch_idx + 1) * dim' universally fails for all 256 threads in this extra iteration. This makes the mutation semantically equivalent—it adds an iteration that performs no observable work regardless of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE: The extra iteration is guarded by a structural boundary check that fails for all threads regardless of input tensor values. No value-level test can expose a difference because the divergent code path never executes any memory writes.
rounds.recommendations: This mutation demonstrates a common pattern where loop bound mutations are neutralized by inner boundary guards. Mutation testing frameworks should detect when a mutated loop bound's extra iterations are provably unreachable due to inner conditions. Consider implementing static analysis to mark such mutations as equivalent before expensive test execution.
